code: library(terra)  # Distances on a small 10 x 10 grid r <- rast(nrows = 10, ncols = 10, xmin = 0, xmax = 10, ymin = 0, ymax = 10) values(r) <- 1:100  # Built-in decay functions w <- c(   calc_decay(r, method = "gaussian", sigma = 30),   calc_decay(r, method = "exponential", sigma = 0.1),   calc_decay(r, method = "power", sigma = 2),   calc_decay(r, method = "binary", sigma = 50) ) names(w) <- c("gaussian", "exponential", "power", "binary") plot(w)   # A custom decay function receives the distances and its own arguments gaussian_power <- function(distance, sigma = 30, power = 2, ...) {   exp(-(distance^2) / (2 * sigma^2)) * distance^(-power) } w_custom <- calc_decay(r, method = gaussian_power, sigma = 30, power = 1.5)  # A declared kernel records its meaning, bounds and fixed arguments plateau <- decay_kernel(   function(distance, sigma, plateau = 5) {     ifelse(distance <= plateau, 1, exp(-(distance - plateau)^2 / (2 * sigma^2)))   },   name = "plateau", parameter = "scale", args = list(plateau = 5) ) w_plateau <- calc_decay(r, method = plateau, sigma = 10)  # One layer per facility gives one layer of weights per facility distances <- rast(replicate(3, r)) names(distances) <- c("facility1", "facility2", "facility3") weights <- calc_decay(distances, method = "gaussian", sigma = 30)

text: original Two-Step Floating Catchment Area (2SFCA) method operates two steps: Step 1: facility j: * Define catchment area within threshold distance/time * Sum population demand locations within catchment * Calculate supply--demand ratio Rj = Sj/sum(Pi) Step 2: demand location : * Define catchment area within threshold distance/time * Sum facility ratios Rj within catchment * Final accessibility score Ai = sum(Rj) Key characteristics: 1. Binary catchment areas (within threshold = 1, beyond = 0) 2. Equal weights locations within catchment 3. normalization demand weights 4. Single threshold value steps Limitations addressed later methods: * distance decay within catchments * Artificial barriers catchment boundaries * Potential demand overestimation overlapping areas
